findings.title: Journal page error state has no retry
findings.steps: Open /journal while the API is down or returns an error (e.g. 5xx).
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that refetches without a reload.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown; there is no retry control (no refresh is taken from useApiFetch). The only way to recover is to edit the search box or reload.
findings.evidence: pages/journal.vue destructures only data/error/status from useApiFetch and renders <AlertMessage v-if="loadError"> with no button.

findings.title: Plant page journal load error has no retry
findings.steps: Open a plant while GET /api/journal?plant_id=… fails.
findings.actual: 'Could not load the journal.' alert with no retry; refreshJournal is only called after adding/deleting an entry.
findings.evidence: pages/plants/[id].vue Journal section: AlertMessage v-if=journalLoadError, no button.

findings.title: Requests have no timeout; a hung API leaves 'Saving…' / 'Loading entries…' forever
findings.steps: Make the API hang (accept connection, never respond) and add, edit or delete an entry, or search on /journal.
findings.expected: Request fails after 10 s with a visible error and the buttons re-enable.
findings.actual: useApiClient/useApiFetch pass no timeout to $fetch, so the button stays disabled showing 'Saving…' (or the list shows 'Loading entries…') indefinitely.
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts: $fetch.create({baseURL, credentials, headers, onResponseError}) – no timeout option; new journal code uses these clients unchanged.

findings.title: Retrying an add after a timeout/lost response creates duplicate journal entries
findings.steps: Submit a new entry; the server stores it but the response is lost/slow and the client errors; click 'Add entry' again.
findings.actual: Each POST inserts a new row; there is no idempotency key or duplicate check, so retrying creates a second identical entry.
findings.evidence: routers/journal.py create_entry does a plain INSERT; the form keeps the text after an error so the user naturally retries.

findings.title: Emoji count double: an entry the server accepts cannot be typed or edited in the form
findings.where: Plant detail journal form / edit in place
findings.steps: POST an entry with 500 emoji (accepted, 201 – server counts code points). Open the plant and click Edit on it, then Save without changes. Also try typing 300 emoji in New entry.
findings.expected: Client and server agree on the 500-character limit; an existing valid entry can be re-saved.
findings.actual: The textarea maxlength and the counter use UTF-16 length, so emoji count as 2: the counter shows '-500 characters left' and Save is refused with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.'; new entries are cut off at 250 emoji.
findings.evidence: API: POST body='🌱'*500 → 201 (entry id 6 on Tomato). JournalEntryForm.vue uses form.body.length and :maxlength=500 for the limit.

findings.title: Huge ids return 500 Internal Server Error on journal endpoints
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (plain text, not JSON) – SQLite integer overflow.
findings.evidence: All four requests answered 'Internal Server Error [500]'. No upper bound on plant_id/entry_id.

findings.title: Journal date accepts year 0001 and any ancient date
findings.steps: POST {"plant_id":1,"entry_on":"0001-01-01","body":"x"} or pick year 0001 in the date input.
findings.expected: Implausible dates refused with a reason (e.g. before plant was planted or before 1900).
findings.actual: 201 Created; entry is stored and shown as '1 Jan 1' at the bottom of the journal.
findings.evidence: API returned 201 with entry_on 0001-01-01. Form has :max but no :min, schema only checks not-in-future.

findings.title: Search over 80 characters returns a raw validation error
findings.steps: Type or paste a search longer than 80 characters.
findings.expected: Input limited to 80 chars (maxlength) or a friendly message, results kept.
findings.actual: API returns 422 and the page replaces the list with 'Q: String should have at most 80 characters'.
findings.evidence: GET /api/journal?q=<81 a's> → 422 string_too_long on query.q; the search input has no maxlength.

findings.title: Search is case-sensitive for non-ASCII letters
findings.steps: Create an entry 'Été chaud, ÉPINARDS'; search 'épinards'.
findings.expected: Matches regardless of case, like ASCII search does ('tomato' matches 'Tomato').
findings.actual: No results; only 'Épinards' matches. SQLite LIKE folds only ASCII case.

findings.title: Deleting an entry already deleted (retry after timeout / other tab) shows an error and leaves the stale entry
findings.steps: Delete an entry in one tab, then delete the same entry in another tab (or retry after a timed-out delete).
findings.expected: Treated as done; the entry disappears from the list.
findings.actual: DELETE returns 404 and the page shows 'Journal entry not found.' while the stale entry stays listed (list is not refreshed on error).
findings.evidence: Second DELETE /api/journal/4 → 404 {"detail":"Journal entry not found."}; removeEntry only refreshes on success.

findings.title: Plant journal silently truncated at 500 entries
findings.steps: Give a plant more than 500 entries.
findings.actual: Only the newest 500 are fetched (limit=500) while the badge shows the full count; older entries cannot be seen, edited or deleted.

findings.title: Back/forward navigation does not update the journal search
findings.steps: Search 'tomato', then navigate in the app and use Back, or change ?q= in the URL via in-app navigation.
findings.expected: Search box and results follow the URL.
findings.actual: search ref is initialised from route.query.q once and never watches the route, so URL and displayed results can disagree.
findings.evidence: pages/journal.vue: watch(search → router.replace) only one direction.

findings.title: 'Today' is checked against the server's date, not the user's
findings.steps: As a user in a timezone ahead of the server (e.g. UTC+12 in the morning), add an entry dated today (the form's default).
findings.actual: Server's date.today() is still yesterday, so it answers 422 'Journal date cannot be in the future.' for the default date.
findings.evidence: schemas.JournalEntryIn.not_in_future uses server-local date.today(); form defaults to browser-local todayIso().
